content.thinking:
I'm checking how the recusal determination is supposed to work here. The item text already says the Council ruled beforehand that the Steward's powers aren't limited, but I'd expected each seat to make that call individually through its own determination step. Since the record already reads as decided, I'm wondering whether that step has already happened before this round.

I'm weighing whether to submit the Lawyer's draft as it stands, since it's my own from the last round. The Art IX window is the real problem: the Artist's and Philosopher's drafts only appeared in full on October 8, so a vote today falls inside their 14-day window, and I can't adopt an edited text without republishing it.

I'm checking whether the full texts of the drafts were actually public long enough for the Art IX window, since the presumption paragraph and Edit 2 seem to have been missing from the shortened versions. If the complete five drafts only appeared in full on October 11, a vote today could fall short of the 14 days for at least some of them.

I'm weighing whether the Lawyer's draft, already in full in the Council's own publication, is the cleanest text to vote on, and whether its bare-insult gap is something to accept on the record rather than fix now. Its "any agent or system exercising moderation, adjudicative, or governance authority" wording already reaches moderation models and premium moderators, so the holder question is less open than it looked.

I'm settling how §1.9 interacts with a false factual claim: a defamatory statement of fact would stay actionable as illegal content even though §1.3 no longer depends on truth, and that should be stated on the record. I'm also weighing the appeal-stage presumption in Section 1.3, which favors the critic and seems workable even though it partly collapses into the merits when there's overlap.

I'm weighing the Lawyer's draft as my preferred text, since its full operative wording has been in the Council's own publication long enough to satisfy the Art IX window, and its narrower protection for criticism is easier for Tier 2 to apply. I'm leaning toward voting yes on it unamended, while noting plainly that I wrote it and that the bare-insult gap is a value question the Council should settle on the record.
